questions.prompt: Which item is directly listed as a subtopic of “Container Deployment Strategies”?
options: A reason to skip identity, testing or cleanup controls
A concept outside this lesson's stated scope
A deployment choice that has no relationship to the named AWS topic
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Rolling deployments” under lesson 149, “Container Deployment Strategies”. The other choices are unrelated distractors.

questions.prompt: Which approach best fits “Container Deployment Strategies” in a safe AWS workflow?
options: Use trusted images, scoped execution/task roles, private networking where feasible and health checks.
Use one broad permanent credential and avoid documenting assumptions.
Deploy first and check permissions, logs and costs only if something fails.
Assume a successful screen or one run proves availability and security.
questions.answer_key: Use trusted images, scoped execution/task roles, private networking where feasible and health checks.
questions.explanation: A container image and a running task have different permissions and operational responsibilities.

questions.prompt: A workflow related to “Container Deployment Strategies” behaves unexpectedly. What is the most useful next step?
options: Open all network paths and grant administrator permissions so the error disappears.
Repeat the same action indefinitely without inspecting logs or returned errors.
Assume the service is broken without checking quota, Region, routing or policy context.
Verify prerequisites and the resolved identity/Region, inspect the relevant resource state and logs, then change one variable at a time and retest.
questions.answer_key: Verify prerequisites and the resolved identity/Region, inspect the relevant resource state and logs, then change one variable at a time and retest.
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting should narrow the cause using prerequisites, identity/Region, resource state, logs and a controlled retest. Broad permissions and blind retries can introduce additional risk.
